discretionary_calls.rule: Class words matched whole-word, case-insensitive; "pathologi" alone as a stem (the table writes it so). A prefix reading is computed beside it for sensitivity and never assigns.
"The adjudication line's own commit" = the commit git blame at the pinned commit attributes the line to. The unit is read from THAT commit's tree, at the line's number in that commit.

A quoted phrase must grep back to exactly one line OTHER THAN the adjudication line itself: the adjudication line quotes the phrase, so counting it would make "exactly one" unreachable for any surviving source.

A path:line locator is resolved at the adjudication commit by trying, in order, the path as written and under exo_memory/, consonance/tools/, consonance/hooks/, consonance/src-tauri/src/, dev/shell/hooks/, dev/shell/, dev/. More than one existing resolution = ambiguous.
A path:line RANGE (a-b, a≠b) locates a passage, not a sentence: not a locator. A range a-a is line a.
A line with several locators is a member only if they all resolve to ONE distinct line; two or more distinct lines = ambiguous, excluded.

"Locates the erroneous sentence" is applied MECHANICALLY: a resolved locator is taken as locating it. No semantic check that the located line is the error rather than, e.g., the correction it quotes. Every member carries its locator and text so the non-author check can audit this.
C3's surface feature "a sentence ending in ?" = a "?" followed by whitespace, end of line, or closing punctuation.
S-UNADJ "same author's section" = the block between the nearest markdown headers (lines starting with #) around the unit in a .md file; the whole file otherwise.
S-UNADJ "within 7 days" = the candidate line's blame committer-time within 7 days of the unit line's, both at the unit's commit.
S-UNADJ candidates must be at least 3 lines from the member line, so the two ±1 units never overlap.
S-UNADJ "not cited by any universe line" = its text is not the text of any universe line and not the text of any universe line's resolved locator.
